transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I... well, my husband thought I should come in. It's just that at work—I'm a teacher—I've been noticing things. The morning announcements, and some of the staff emails... I just get this feeling they're actually coded messages directed at me. My colleagues try to tell me they're just standard emails sent to the whole staff, but... I just can't shake the feeling.
Have there been times when you felt unusually high, euphoric, or intensely energetic?
No... I don't think so. I just feel like I normally do. I haven't had anything like that.
Have you been hearing voices when no one else is around?

I... well, sometimes. I guess. Just when it's really quiet. Like at the house, or after the classroom empties out for the day. I'll hear... a woman. She just says my name, or makes a quick comment about what I'm doing. It sounds clear enough that I've actually answered out loud before... before realizing no one else is in the room.
Do you ever feel like other people can hear or know your thoughts, even when you haven’t said them out loud?
No, I... I don't think so. I haven't noticed anything like that. My thoughts are... they're just my own.
Have these experiences been going on for more than a month?

Yes... it's been longer than a month. I suppose... maybe around four months now. Just... the voice I mentioned. And... well, some worries I've been having about... coded messages. But yes, about four months.
Have you found yourself losing interest in things you used to enjoy?

I... suppose you could say that. I mean, I still care about my students, of course. And my friends. It's not that I don't care. But... for many months now, it just feels like the warmth and the drive have sort of... drained out of me. 

I've just let things slide. My book club, the theater planning at school... even simple phone calls, really. Unless someone pushes me to do it, I just... don't.
Have people told you that your speech has been hard to follow or that you jump from one idea to another in a way that doesn’t make sense to them?
No, I... I haven't heard that. People usually understand me fine. I just... I don't talk as much as I used to, maybe. But when I do, it's... it makes sense.
Because of these experiences, have you been having trouble doing your job or managing things day to day?

I suppose... a little. I mean, I am still teaching. I haven't stopped working. But... I have needed some of my coworkers to step in and cover parts of the project lessons for me lately. And... well, just to help me get through the planning meetings. 

And outside of school... I think I already mentioned the book club and the theater. I've just stopped being reliable for those. Or the neighborhood events, really. I just... I can't seem to manage them right now.
From the time these problems first began, has it been six months yet?

Yes... it's been longer than that. 

I suppose... this overall change in how I work and think... and connect with people... it's been going on since my youngest left for college. That was about a year and two months ago.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports persistent persecutory/reference delusions (coded messages directed at her) and recurrent auditory hallucinations (hearing a woman's voice commenting/calling her name), with negative symptoms including reduced motivation, diminished emotional warmth, and social withdrawal. There is clear functional decline in work and social roles, and the disturbance has persisted for more than 6 months overall with at least 1 month of active psychotic symptoms. No manic symptoms were endorsed. This presentation is most consistent with paranoid schizophrenia.
